title: Gulfport Mississippi Tornado Damage
description: A man documents the damage in the aftermath of a tornado along U.S. Highway 90 in Gulfport, Mississippi, April 14, 1980. (U.S. Army video)

transcript.text: Gulfport just off of highway 90. Most of the damage is restricted to roof damage. There's
a lot of fine debris such as air conditioning, duct work, a lot of broken windows but mainly
minor exterior damage. This is another view of the same motel off of highway 90 and Gulf
port. There's a good bit more damage on this side of the motel. As you can see, many of
the front windows were blown out and there also seems to be some structural damage although
it seems to be minor and on the exterior. Structurally the building seems sound but obviously a lot
of the contents were ruined by the rain afterwards. This shot is at the same motel and it's taking
a prox just one day after the tornado hit. Already repairmen are starting to do minor clean
up work on the roof of the motel. This is a view of the Fountainhead Booth Motel just
off of highway 90 and Gulfport. This is the same motel that was pictured previously. As
you can see, repairmen are still working on the roof which appears to be the main portion
of the damage to the motel. Structurally the other than the roof that doesn't appear
to be too much damage. This is a view of the Westside Community Center in the West Gulfport
area just off of highway 90. As you can see, part of the area was just totally demolished.
Tennis court, defense law on the tennis court was pretty well torn up. Several trees were
completely uprooted by the winds and there's quite a bit of debris seen up in the trees.
One building structure itself was completely demolished. Another building structure had
a portion of the roof torn off but it appears to be in pretty good shape otherwise. The
building that was torn down appears to have been a small recreation center due to the
roof of the International House of Pancakes about one block from the Westside Community
Center. The only apparent damage seems to be a number of aluminum sheets torn off of
the roof. There doesn't appear to be any major structural damage other than the aluminum
sheeting itself. This is a view of the front of the Westside Community Center as shot from
highway 90. As you can see, there apparently was some sort of patio or roof facade originally
at the front of the community center which has been blown away. It's been totally destroyed.
The building itself seems to be in fairly good shape other than some cedar shingles that
have been blown off. There does not appear to be any major structural damage. Some windows
were blown out and there was some apparent water damage inside other than that. There
was not any damage. This is a view of the power company repairing some of their down power
lines. This location is just west of the Westside Community Center just off of highway 90.
Apparently the lines were not damaged too greatly but they are making some repairs. Now
you are now looking at Acorn Arms Apartments Local apartment structure had the woofrown
off. It's not evident from this view but the north wing had quite a bit of extensive
roof damage. The structural damage was not too severe but the roof was completely blown
off. Residents are trying to dry out personal belongings from the inside. This is a view
of the Mississippi Highway Patrol Office in Gulfport which is just north of the Westside
Community Center. The damage seems to be rather minor and appears to be mostly roof damage.
You can see some of the insulation laying around. You can also see debris from fallen trees. The
community in the neighborhood appears to have some slight roof damage but it once again appears
to be minor also. This is the backside of the Westside Community Center just across from
the Highway Patrol Office. You can see numerous amounts of debris around the area mostly from
roofs of houses in the area. This is a view of the neighborhood just north of the Westside
Community Center. The debris in the yard is typical of the debris in this particular neighborhood.
As you can see it's mostly asphalt shingles. The damage once again appears to be restricted
to roofs blown off by the heavy winds. This is a view of a resident just north of the
Highway Patrol Station. Very little damage other than the fact that apparently one column
was blown out causing the roof to fall. The house doesn't have any other damage other
than a few shingles missing. We're panning over to a house next to it where the awning
was ripped out but this appears to be typical of the area just around the Westside Community
Center. It seems to be some minor damage here and there's some roof damage and some structural
damage. Very little structural damage, mostly minor damage. This is a view of a resident
also in the area of the Westside Community Center. Some supports were blown down on a
roof causing it to fall on top of a car. This is just an isolated instance however because
most of the damage was not very severe in this area and it's basically pretty minor.
The Mitchell entire center on Highway 90, approximately two blocks west of the Westside
Community Center sustained quite a bit of damage. As you can see cement block and brick
wall, brick veneer walls were blown out completely. The entire roof was completely removed from
the tire center and basically there appears to be some structural damage on the remaining
walls. The center itself appears to be more west and completely damaged. This is a view
of a local motel unit just west of the Mitchell entire center on Highway 90. It appears that
the majority of the roof of this unit was completely torn off by the wind as you can see by the
blown wet insulation all over the area. Some cement blocks have been blown off to indicate
that some of the wall connected to the roof was also damaged but basically the building
appears to be structurally sound other than the roof itself. There are quite a bit of
damage to the interiors of the room into the personal belongings inside of the room.
This is another view of the electric company making repairs the day after the storm. It
appears that there were not that many power lines down as a result of the storm but it's
kind of difficult to see since the crews have been out so early working. This is a shot
of a local apartment complex just to the east of the motel unit shown before. Once again
this appears to be restricted to mostly roof damage. No structural damage is evident. This
is a convenience store just to the west of the Mitchell entire center. Once again it
also has had its roof completely blown off. It appears to be quite a bit of damage to the
roof. This is a view of a local service station just off of highway 90 and you can see two
cars were completely demolished by steel sign. This is an indication of the forces of the tornado
winds here at Gulfport. Also there's a roof that's completely been blown off of the service
station. Once again structural damage seems to be only restricted to that which was tied
to the roof that does not appear to be any major structural damage. The strength of the
wind is evident from the bending of the steel columns here on the support sign. This is more
damage along highway 90 in Gulfport. It should be noted that the major damage in this area
seems to be restricted to about an eight block area along highway 90 and approximately two
blocks north of highway 90. This is a fast food chain. It appears to have all the windows
blown out and some roof damage but other than that it appears to be rather minor. This is
a view of the Waffle House along highway 90 in Gulfport. As you can see damage here is
restricted mostly to glass panels being blown out and some roof damage. This is typical
of any establishment along the area that had mostly a glass front. It's not conclusive
as to whether or not the damage was from flying debris or from actually the force of the winds
however it is similar to the other damages in the area. This is a good shot of power
company crews the day after the storm attempting to clean up debris which is keeping down power
lines. This is going to be a wide-angle shot of the western edge of the area affected by
the tornado. This shot is taken to just south of highway 90. It should be noted that most
of the damage seems to be restricted to a commercial area along highway 90 for about eight blocks
section. There are some residential sections just north of this area for about a block
due to that also have been affected. However the majority of the destruction appears to
be commercial. This is another view of the commercial district along highway 90. In the
meantime we heard rumors that there was extensive damage as the Gulfport airport. We checked
them out and we also talked to the airport manager and we did not come up with any major damage
at all. There were some minor damage to buildings and maybe one or two planes we saw that were
damaged but basically according to the airport manager the damage was rather slight. We
are now proceeding east on highway 90 towards Mobile and after leaving the damaged area the
Westside Community Center which you are looking at now appears to be the area that was hard
to sit. This is not at all typical of the damage this was by far the greatest destruction.
I might also be noted that some of the debris that was noticed in some of the residential
areas just north of here turned out to actually be debris from the Community Center which was
blown as much as two blocks away. Once again this is some more damage along highway 90.
The shot is taken from the south side of highway 90. It should be noticed that we are repeating
some of our shots back from away and we are trying to pan across and give you a better
idea of the damage. This is the Fountainhead Motel which has been shot previously.
